chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is the one from whom his neighbour is safe of his deeds.' I said, 'And what are his deeds?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His injustice and his harshness.'

key_terms.بَوَائِق: Deeds or actions, specifically evil or harmful ones in this context
key_terms.غَشْم: Harshness, rudeness, or coarseness in conduct

ai.seo_question: What are the specific deeds from which a neighbour should be safe according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the essence of faith through social integrity, specifying that a true believer is one whose neighbor feels secure from his 'bawa'iq' (plurality of evils). He clarifies these evils as 'zulm' (injustice) and 'ghashm' (harshness or coarseness of character), highlighting that spiritual belief is validated by the absence of social friction and moral roughness in daily interactions. This definition underscores the Shia emphasis on 'adab' (etiquette) and justice as tangible markers of Iman.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘A Momin is the one from whom his neighbour is safe of his deeds’. I said, ‘And what are his deeds?’ Heasws said: ‘His injustice and his harshness’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Muhammad ibn Hafs from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shami who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once speaking to the people who had filled up his house said, ‘You must take notice that those who fail to maintain good relations with their neighbors are not of our people and followers.’”
